messages.subject: Negative learning rate for bandit2arm model
parts:
Hi!

My name is Simon, I'm a PhD student at CIMH in Mannheim, Germany, and I'm doing research on interactions of pain and reward.

I have an experiment in which a drug manipulation even seems to reverse operant learning in a simple 2 armed-bandit task (using pain relief as a reward).

Therefore, I tried to model a negative learning rate. To achieve this, I edited the stan file (bandit2arm_delta.stan) and set vector<lower=-1, upper=1>A. Following the update (#107) made on the choiceRT_ddm model to facilitate a negative drift rate, I also changed A[i] = Phi_approx(mu_pr[1] + sigma[1] * A_pr[i]); to A[i] = mu_pr[1] + sigma[1] * A_pr[i];.
This model runs but it gives some strange results: the model plot shows me an estimated mu_A with a mean of around 0.5 while the single subjects' estimated A parameters are all in a range [-0.1, 0.1]. How can this be?
I have also set up a bandit2arm model with more parameters (comparable to the bandit4arm_4par model) and allowed the parameters R(reward sensitivity) and P (punishment sensitivity) to vary between negative and positive values. This model gives me a lot divergent transitions, even with a high number of iterations.
So I wonder if I misunderstood the way the models are set up in Stan..

Especially the first of these models seems to model the data quite well! Running a simulation with the obtained subjectwise parameters I can reproduce the number of correct choices (choice of the arm with a better net outcome) quite nicely...
Thus, I'd really like to get the models running and any ideas/input on this is highly appreciated!
Thanks a lot!

Best wishes,

Simon


P.S.: I also opened an issue at Github before I stumbled across this google group. I apologize if that was the wrong place to seek for support and I'm happy to close the issue if that was the case!

messages.author: 47d1400f432367d7
messages.subject: Re: Negative learning rate for bandit2arm model
parts:
Hi Simon,

This sounds like an interesting application! 

My first thought is that, you may have missed the part in the "generated quantities" block where you need to change:

"mu_A = Phi_approx(mu_pr[1])" to

"mu_A = mu_pr[1]"

in order to reflect the corresponding change you made in the transformed parameters block. Actually, given that you are seeing mu_A = .5 (which is what we would expect from the phi_approx transform if the actual mu_p[1] value was around 0), I am pretty sure that is the issue!

I think the issues you are encountering with the negative sensitivity parameters may be that, if the learning rate can also be negative, there is likely an identifiability issue between the sensitivity and learning rate parameters. If you plot person-level (or group-level) pairs plots, do they look highly co-linear? The models could still fit the data well even with this issue, despite the parameters not being recoverable. That would not necessarily explain the divergent transitions, though, but would be a good thing to check. 

(and yes, I think it would be best to close the GitHub issue given that this is related to a modification of the original code)

Best,
Nate

Dear Nate,

thanks for the quick reply!
You were absolutely right, I missed to also change the respective line in the generated quantities block. This solved the issue of the group level parameter which now seems to reflect the single subject parameters for A. Great! Thanks!

For the model in which I allowed the sensitivity parameters to be negative I did deliberately not allow the learning rates (Arew and Apun) to be below zero as I expected that to cause issues. 
Here is what the pairs plot on the group level parameters looks like:
I'd interpret that there is an issue with the separate learning rates that creates issues with the identifiability, correct?
Should I try to model a single learning rate instead?

Thank you!

Best wishes, 
Simon

P.S.: Issue on Github closed..

messages.subject: Re: Negative learning rate for bandit2arm model
parts:
Great! Glad that was a simple fix. 

And thanks for the plot. Could you include the "sigma" parameters (i.e. group-level SDs) in the pairs plot as well? I am wondering if there are any funnels showing up their, which could produce all these divergent transitions. 

As for identifiability, I would say that these actually look good in terms of no extreme trade-offs. It is interesting that some of the samples for the learning rates are so far from the mass of the rest of the posterior, though. Including the SD might be able to help.

Could you also include your Stan code here? 

Best,
Nate

Dear Nate,

However, if I keep parameter restrictions in both, the transformed parameter block (vector<lower=P_min, upper=P_max>[N] P;) and the generated quantities block (vector<lower=-30, upper=30>[N] mu_P;) I get a lot of exceptions and I cannot really run the model:
Chain 1: Exception: validate transformed params: mu_P is 32.2043, but must be less than or equal to 30  (in 'model2a522198448_bandit2arm_delta_5par_negsens' at line 113)

Nevertheless, I am now able to run the model and get reasonable parameter estimates. This does solve my initial issue.
I just wonder if this affects parameter estimation in some way, and if so, if I should worry about this... Any feedback is welcome!

Thanks!

Best wishes, 
Simon

Am 02.03.2021 um 15:49 schrieb Haines, Nathaniel B. <haine...@buckeyemail.osu.edu>:

Hi Simon,

This sounds like an interesting application! 

My first thought is that, you may have missed the part in the "generated quantities" block where you need to change:

"mu_A = Phi_approx(mu_pr[1])" to

"mu_A = mu_pr[1]"

in order to reflect the corresponding change you made in the transformed parameters block. Actually, given that you are seeing mu_A = .5 (which is what we would expect from the  phi_approx transform if the actual mu_p[1] value was around 0), I am pretty sure that is the issue!

I think the issues you are encountering with the negative sensitivity parameters may be that, if the learning rate can also be negative, there is likely an identifiability issue between the sensitivity and learning rate parameters. If you plot person-level (or group-level) pairs plots, do they look highly co-linear? The models could still fit the data well even with this issue, despite the parameters not being recoverable. That would not necessarily explain the divergent transitions, though, but would be a good thing to check. 

(and yes, I think it would be best to close the GitHub issue given that this is related to a modification of the original code)

Best,
Nate
